recommendation_superseded_by.decision: Later guard-free page-aligned execution finds a one-request RX 7900 XTX physical ceiling of 129,024 tokens, with first failure at the next 256-token page, and extends bounded mixed_v1 BF16-vs-INT8 quality to 129,024/16 on W7900. The four-request 114,688-token natural soak remains the strongest repeated XTX evidence. Capacity and quality fields below preserve this artifact's 2026-08-15 historical measurements.

decision: Retain the bounded exact-prefill implementation and qualify pure FP32-scale per-token/head INT8 KV as an explicit Qwen3.8 single-request AR capacity route. This historical packet established memory savings, overlapping BF16-prefill sample bands, faster eager INT8 AR decode, and completed rows through 114,688 tokens. Its capacity and bounded-quality frontier is superseded by the linked 2026-08-16 artifact; BF16 remains the supported/default route, long pure INT8 remains behind the explicit unverified-long gate, pure INT8 decode is not admitted to the HIP graph, and exact natural B3 MTP remains slower than true AR.

implementation.safety: The shared oracle is selected only with full-prompt hidden ownership and layer-outer scheduling. A fail-closed guard rejects shared ownership if allocation drift re-enters chunk-outer execution. BF16, short mirrored INT8, and memory-negative hybrid layouts preserve their prior route.

bounded_change_vs_prior_int8.interpretation: The decode sample ranges overlap at their boundary and were measured in different sessions. The binding result is the exact 1.613554-GiB peak reduction and non-regression versus the supported BF16-graph decode route.

matched_runtime.interpretation: Bounded INT8 prefill is within 0.051% of the matched BF16 graph-route median and the prefill sample ranges overlap. Eager INT8 decode is 6.50% faster than BF16 graph. The route therefore meets the fixed-shape AR memory/decode gate without a measurable prefill regression.

protocol.pass_rule: HTTP 200, one generated token, /ready true after request, and clean teardown

server_capacity.interpretation: 112 Ki is the highest completed row and the later natural-request soak promotes it for the explicit dedicated-c1 contract. The 120-Ki row was not executed because a configured startup guard blocked it; the first actual runtime failure is the 128-Ki eager-warmup HIP OOM. 96 Ki remains an optional extra-headroom point. Only 64 Ki has a representative long-context quality row, and all long pure-INT8 rows still require the explicit unverified-long gate.

natural_mtp.decision: Correctness and transaction admission pass, but pure-INT8 serial-exact target verification is not a speed path. Do not advertise INT8 MTP or change the BF16/default natural-MTP row.

limitations: The 64K/96K/112K server prompts repeat token 9707 to fix memory shape. They are capacity and lifecycle evidence, not representative quality or throughput rows.
The complete natural/category quality gates cover 512 and 4K. The 64K long-context gate covers only mixed_v1; no representative 96K or 112K quality suite was run.
112K leaves only 0.662 GiB at sampled request high water and is one clean request, so it is an observed ceiling row rather than a recommended production setting.
Pure INT8 is eager-only for AR decode graph capture and slows serial-exact B3 MTP. The retained BF16 graph/MTP routes remain the default.

The full natural MTP artifact's generic provenance field says kv_dtype=bf16 because the committed suite has no INT8 target CLI. The hashed disposable wrapper replaces only target session construction with explicit FP32-scale INT8; the row's target behavior and layout were separately checked before the full run.
This qualification covers one active request, no prefix-cache retention, and no concurrent c>1 server ownership.
